summary: Build practical investment management skills in allocation, portfolio risk, performance, and governance. Review the five-day course and enrol.
lede: Investment management is the structured process of aligning portfolio decisions with client objectives, constraints, and risk tolerance. For portfolio managers, investment analysts, and wealth managers, the course focuses on constructing and monitoring portfolios through a documented investment process. Participants practise modelling asset allocation, measuring risk, evaluating managers, and preparing performance attribution and investment committee reports using spreadsheet-based analysis.
audienceIntro: Investment management training suits professionals who already work with portfolios, financial analysis, clients, or investment governance and want to connect theory with repeatable operating outputs.
prerequisites: Working knowledge of financial markets, investment products, and basic portfolio terminology is expected. You should have experience reading investment reports or supporting portfolio, wealth, treasury, fund, or performance activities. No programming is required. Spreadsheet familiarity is useful, but the practical exercises use provided templates and datasets. Advanced topics such as Black-Litterman, Monte Carlo simulation, and AI-assisted research are taught at operational application or conceptual awareness level, not technical engineering level.
